Creating Communities

It seems to me that the biggest hurdle of the “alt right” is a lack of IRL community. Discord servers are great, but I reckon most people need a community of like minded people in meatspace to motivate them. But there is a significant signalling penalty that prevents these communities from forming. Everybody is afraid of revealing their powerlevel. Even if you can attract the right kind of people, you still have the risk of infiltrators; people who can destroy a group and the lives of everyone in it (hyperbole, but not really).

I have devised a method of community building that will minimise such risks. Based on the clandestine cell system, but without any hierachical requirements. The aim is to create a system that (while imperfect) converges toward large, shill free groups. I am trying to ensure that entry into a group is dependent on a communal trust, built on repeated interactions.

This system is built on top of a concept called ‘squads’. A squad is a group of one or more people who have vetted each other. Two squads can merge into a larger squad. This should only be done if you are certain that all the members of the other squad are trustworthy. Squads can be disbanded or individuals dispelled from the squad. There are no leaders.

The Process

  1. You are assigned to a squad containing only yourself (the trivial squad)

  2. After there are suffient squads available, a squad of similar size will be chosen for you too match with at random. This new squad will not contain any members you have been previously matched with.

  3. You will be given an encripted channel through which to chat, and an

email address for planning the meetup (time, date and place).

a) meetup again

b) reject match

If you ditch the meetup, that’s an automatic match reject for wasting time.
